ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=2\angle B$, and $CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$. If $AD=2$, $BD=3$, what is the length of $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}:\\
Since $CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACD=\angle BCD=\frac{1}{2}\angle ACB$.\\
Given $\angle ACB=2\angle B$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACD=\angle B$.\\
Considering $\triangle ADC$ and $\triangle ACB$, we have\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle ACD=\angle B \\
\angle A=\angle A
\end{array}\right.$\\
Hence, $\triangle ADC\sim \triangle ACB$\\
which implies $\frac{AD}{AC}=\frac{AC}{AB}$, i.e.,\\
$AC^{2}=AD\cdot AB$.\\
Given $AD=2, BD=3$,\\
it follows that $AB=AD+BD=5$\\
and thus $AC^{2}=AD\cdot AB=10$.\\
Since the length of a segment is a positive number, $AC=\sqrt{10}$. Therefore, the solution is $AC=\boxed{\sqrt{10}}$.
